title: Student Dataclass Ranking

visible.label: Sorts highest average first with ascending student_id tie-break
visible.expectedDisplay: Higher avg first; tie broken by student_id ascending
visible.script:
s1 = StudentRecord("Zara", "S02", [80, 90])
s2 = StudentRecord("Amy", "S01", [85, 85])
s3 = StudentRecord("Liam", "S03", [95, 95])
ranked = rank_students([s1, s2, s3])
assert [r.student_id for r in ranked] == ["S03", "S01", "S02"]

visible.label: Empty scores computes 0.0 average safely
visible.script:
p = StudentRecord("Pat", "S10")
assert p.scores == []
assert p.average() == 0.0

hidden.label: Two instances do not share mutable default scores list
hidden.script:
a = StudentRecord("A", "1")
b = StudentRecord("B", "2")
a.scores.append(100)
assert b.scores == []

hidden.label: Does not mutate input list passed to rank_students
hidden.script:
s1 = StudentRecord("B", "S2", [70])
s2 = StudentRecord("A", "S1", [90])
orig = [s1, s2]
out = rank_students(orig)
assert out == [s2, s1]
assert orig == [s1, s2]

hints: Use @dataclass with `scores: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)` so dataclass allows mutable defaults safely.
Sort a new list with `sorted(records, key=lambda r: (-r.average(), r.student_id))`.
